consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is a counterfeit covenant community that claims the identity and privileges of God’s people while opposing God/Christ and persecuting the faithful (chiefly Rev 2:9; 3:9 ‘synagogue of Satan’ for those who say they are Jews and are not, linked to Ps 22:16 assembly of the wicked as the hostile crowd around the suffering Messiah).
book_summary: Book defines it as a counterfeit congregation claiming covenant standing while gathered against the covenant’s Lord—a spiritual identity fixed by allegiance and rejection of Messiah, never ancestry—with the pattern displayed by Korah’s company, the brood of vipers/children of the Devil, the assembly surrounding the Messiah, and those who say they are Jews but are not.
consensus_core_identification: false claimants to covenant people status who oppose God/Christ and persecute the faithful
book_core_identification: counterfeit congregation claiming covenant standing yet gathered against the covenant’s Lord (spiritual allegiance, not ancestry)
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates Korah’s rebellion (Num 16/14), ‘brood of vipers’ (Matt 3/12), and the composite gathering of Acts 4:27 as primary displays of the same pattern; consensus keeps those peripheral or unmentioned and centers the term on the Revelation polemic plus Ps 22, treating broader false-church applications as secondary/homiletic.
rationale: Minimum cores are equivalent (counterfeit covenant assembly opposing the Lord/Messiah). Extra scriptural types and the explicit ‘never by ancestry’ clause do not replace the referent; they enlarge the set of recognized cases and tighten the boundary condition, producing a refined extension rather than divergence or novelty.
strongest_objection: Traditional linkage of the exact phrase ‘synagogue of Satan’ is almost exclusively to Rev 2–3 (and secondarily Ps 22); folding Korah and the Matthean vipers in as co-equal displays may be viewed as an over-extension of the term’s established range.
